title: Japan's MMX launches Mon. Oct. 19 to grab a piece of Phobos
description:
Phobos, the larger moon of Mars, drops about six feet closer to Mars every hundred years, and in about fifty million years it will crash into Mars or break up into a ring. On Monday, Oct. 19, 2026, Japan launches MMX on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima to land on Phobos, collect a sample and fly it back to Earth. No mission has ever returned a sample from Mars or its moons, and that sample could finally show where the two moons came from.
